# Writing Hooks

> Scope: authoring Claude Code `hooks.json` plus the hook scripts it points at.
> **Hook event vocabularies are per-tool and are NOT 1:1 mappable.** Claude uses
> `PreToolUse`/`PostToolUse`/`Stop` and friends; Codex overlaps with Claude but
> adds `PostCompact` and `SubagentStart`; Antigravity/Gemini decomposes events
> differently, into `Before*`/`After*` variants over Agent/Model/Tool. What DOES
> transfer across tools: script design principles — idempotency, fail-open
> behavior, exit codes, portable paths. What does NOT transfer: event names and
> config locations. All config JSON in this file is Claude-shaped; Codex's TOML
> config is not covered beyond this note. See also
> [writing-plugins](../vibe-writing-plugins/SKILL.md) for plugin architecture and
> [writing-rules](../vibe-writing-rules/SKILL.md) — rules are simpler than hooks, but
> static.

## 1. Three Hook Types

| Type | What it does | When to use | Complexity |
|---|---|---|---|
| `command` | Runs a shell script that reads JSON from stdin | Deterministic checks: file existence, JSON validation, regex | Medium |
| `prompt` | Injects text into Claude's context | Advisory: reminders, context injection, style guidance | Low |
| `agent` | Spawns a verification agent | Complex verification: code quality, semantic analysis, multi-file checks | High |

### Type Selection Flowchart

```
Is the check deterministic (regex / file-exists / JSON schema)?
  yes --> command
  no  --> Does it need AI judgment?
            yes --> agent
            no  --> prompt
```

### Command Hook Example

```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PreToolUse": [
      {
        "matcher": "Write|Edit",
        "hooks": [
          {
            "type": "command",
            "command": "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/check-loc.sh",
            "timeout": 10000
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Contract: the command script receives JSON on stdin (the tool name and its
parameters) and must write JSON to stdout.

### Prompt Hook Example

```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "UserPromptSubmit": [
      {
        "hooks": [
          {
            "type": "prompt",
            "prompt": "Reminder: this project uses conventional commit messages and keeps modules under 300 lines."
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

### Agent Hook Example

```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PostToolUse": [
      {
        "matcher": "Write|Edit",
        "hooks": [
          {
            "type": "agent",
            "agent": "Check the modified file against the project conventions and report any violations."
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Config shape: the top-level key is `hooks`, mapping each event name to an array
of entries; each entry has an optional `matcher` plus a `hooks` array of typed
hook objects.

## 2. Blocking vs Advisory

### Blocking

A blocking hook is `PreToolUse` with a deny decision — it prevents the tool from
executing. Use it for hard quality gates. The output JSON:

```json
{
  "hookSpecificOutput": {
    "permissionDecision": "deny",
    "permissionDecisionReason": "src/big.js is 512 lines; the limit is 300. Split the file before writing."
  }
}
```

The reason must be a human-readable message with specifics.

Block when: tests must pass before a commit; a file exceeds the size limit; a
required config field is missing; a dangerous operation is detected (force push,
drop table).

### Advisory

An advisory hook is `PostToolUse` with a message — it adds context after the
action has happened. Use it for suggestions and reminders. The output JSON:

```json
{
  "hookSpecificOutput": {
    "message": "You created a new module without tests — consider adding a spec file."
  }
}
```

Advise when: suggesting related actions (run tests, update docs); convention
reminders; surfacing contextual info; warning without blocking.

### Decision Matrix

| Situation | Block or advise | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Test failure on commit | Block | Broken tests are never committed |
| File over the LOC limit | Block | It's a hard limit |
| Missing JSDoc on an export | Advise | Nice-to-have |
| No tests for a new file | Advise | A reminder, not a gate |
| Force push to main | Block | Destructive and irreversible |
| Large file creation, > 500 lines | Advise | Might be intentional or generated |

Rule of thumb: block only what a code review would reject; advise everything
else.

## 3. Event Selection Guide

| Event | When it fires | Common uses |
|---|---|---|
| `PreToolUse` | Before a tool executes | Block dangerous ops, validate inputs, check preconditions |
| `PostToolUse` | After a tool succeeds | Follow-up actions, lint changed files, update state |
| `PostToolUseFailure` | After a tool fails | Error recovery, suggest alternatives, log failures |
| `UserPromptSubmit` | The user sends a message | Context injection, session setup, mode activation |
| `Stop` | Claude stops responding | Cleanup, summary generation, state persistence |
| `SessionStart` | A session begins | Environment validation, context loading, config checks |

### Event Selection by Goal

| Goal | Event + type |
|---|---|
| Prevent bad writes | `PreToolUse` + matcher `Write\|Edit` + command |
| Lint after an edit | `PostToolUse` + matcher `Write\|Edit` + command |
| Inject project context | `UserPromptSubmit` + prompt |
| Validate env on start | `SessionStart` + command |
| Save a session summary on exit | `Stop` + agent |
| Recover a failed bash call | `PostToolUseFailure` + matcher `Bash` + prompt |

## 4. Matcher Patterns

The `matcher` field holds a regex tested against tool names, and only three
events honor it: `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, and `PostToolUseFailure`.

| Pattern | Matches | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `"Bash"` | Bash only | Guard shell commands |
| `"Write\|Edit"` | Either one | Guard file modifications |
| `"Write"` | File creation only | Creation-specific gates |
| `"Edit"` | Edits only | Edit-specific gates |
| `"Read"` | Read | Track reads |
| `"mcp__.*"` | All MCP calls | Guard external integrations |
| `"mcp__github__.*"` | GitHub MCP tools | GitHub-specific policies |
| `"Task"` | Agent dispatch | Monitor sub-agent launches |
| `".*"` | Everything | Use carefully — fires on every tool call |

### Matcher Testing

Verify every matcher with positive AND negative cases before deploying:

| Matcher | Must match | Must NOT match |
|---|---|---|
| `"Write\|Edit"` | Write, Edit | Bash, Read, WriteFile |
| `"Bash"` | Bash | BashScript, mcp__bash |
| `"mcp__github__.*"` | mcp__github__create_pr | mcp__slack__send |

## 5. Portable Paths

Script paths in hooks.json must always go through `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`,
which the runtime expands to the plugin's install location.

Do this:

```json
"command": "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/check-loc.sh"
```

Not this — an absolute path into one machine's plugin cache fails everywhere
else:

```json
"command": "/Users/me/.claude/plugins/cache/my-plugin@1.0.0/scripts/check-loc.sh"
```

### Script Location Convention

The plugin root holds `hooks/hooks.json` (the definitions) and `scripts/*.sh`
(the hook scripts).

### Script Requirements

1. A shebang line — `#!/usr/bin/env node` for Node scripts, `#!/bin/bash` for
   shell scripts.
2. The executable bit set: `chmod +x scripts/*.sh`.
3. Valid JSON on stdout.
4. Debug logging goes to stderr — stdout is parsed as JSON.

### Worked Script: LOC Gate

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Deny writes to files over 300 lines.
input=$(cat)
echo "check-loc invoked at $(date)" >&2

file_path=$(echo "$input" | jq -r '.toolInput.file_path // empty')
if [ -z "$file_path" ]; then
  # Target path indeterminable — allow and get out of the way.
  echo '{"hookSpecificOutput":{"decision":"allow"}}'
  exit 0
fi

loc=$(wc -l < "$file_path" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
if [ "$loc" -gt 300 ]; then
  echo "{\"hookSpecificOutput\":{\"permissionDecision\":\"deny\",\"permissionDecisionReason\":\"$file_path is $loc lines; the limit is 300.\"}}"
else
  echo '{"hookSpecificOutput":{"decision":"allow"}}'
fi
```

Note the asymmetry: the allow path uses `hookSpecificOutput.decision: "allow"`,
while the deny path uses `permissionDecision`.

## 6. Fail-Open vs Fail-Closed

What should happen when the hook script itself crashes?

### Fail-Open (recommended default)

A crash allows the action to proceed. Safer for advisory hooks and non-critical
checks:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
set +e
output=$("${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/real-check.sh" <<< "$(cat)")
code=$?
if [ "$code" -ne 0 ]; then
  echo '{"hookSpecificOutput":{"decision":"allow"}}'
  exit 0
fi
echo "$output"
```

### Fail-Closed (security-critical only)

A crash denies the action. Same wrapper shape, but a nonzero exit emits a deny
with a reason such as "safety script failed; blocking as a precaution."

### When to Use Each

| Hook purpose | Mode | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| LOC limit | Fail-open | Better to allow one large file than block all writes |
| Style reminder | Fail-open | Non-critical |
| Prevent force push to main | Fail-closed | Destructive — err on the cautious side |
| Secret detection | Fail-closed | Security-critical; must not leak |
| Test runner | Fail-open | Test infra failure shouldn't block development |

## 7. Common Mistakes

| Mistake | Why it's wrong | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Blocking on `PostToolUse` | The action already happened | Use `PreToolUse` for blocking |
| Wrong event case (`pretooluse`) | Event names are case-sensitive | Exact `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, etc. |
| Script not executable | The hook fails silently | `chmod +x scripts/*.sh` |
| Missing shebang | Wrong interpreter runs the script | Add `#!/bin/bash` or `#!/usr/bin/env node` |
| Hardcoded paths | Breaks on any other machine | `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` |
| Stdout pollution | Debug output mixed into the JSON | Log to stderr (`>&2`) |
| No timeout | A slow script blocks Claude indefinitely | `"timeout": 10000` (10 seconds) |
| Matcher too broad (`".*"`) | Fires on every call — performance hit | Narrow to the specific tools |
| No fail-open wrapper | A crash means a broken hook and a frustrated user | Wrap fail-open |

## 8. Quality Checklist

Before deploying a hook, confirm:

- [ ] The chosen event fits the goal.
- [ ] Anything that blocks runs on `PreToolUse`, never on `PostToolUse`.
- [ ] Each matcher has been tried against tool names it must match and names it
      must not.
- [ ] Every script path uses `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`.
- [ ] Every script has a shebang and the executable bit.
- [ ] Scripts emit valid JSON on stdout.
- [ ] Debug output goes to stderr.
- [ ] Every hook makes an explicit fail-open or fail-closed choice.
- [ ] A timeout is set on every hook (10 seconds is the default).
- [ ] Tested with normal input, edge-case input, and missing input.
